Amelia / Mina — thanks. Attaching our initial positions for consideration (summary below; full tracked changes attached).

Subprocessor notice (our proposal):
- Redwood will provide written notice of new subprocessors at least 30 days prior to onboarding for any processing of EEA personal data.
- Customer will have a 30-calendar-day objection window; if objection is raised, parties will engage in good-faith discussions to resolve; failure to resolve allows either party to suspend affected processing for the impacted account.
- For high-risk subprocessors (storage hosting, KMS providers), Redwood will provide additional technical docs upon request.

Transfers:
- Redwood will execute the standard SCCs (or equivalent EU-approved transfer mechanism) where required and provides an EU-US Transfer Addendum for US hosting customers.

KMS / keys:
- We use a combination of Redwood-managed KMS (GCP/AWS/KMS) with support for customer-managed keys for enterprise plans. We are happy to provide architecture diagrams and HSM attestations under an NDA or via our security questionnaire.

Execution:
- Redwood typically executes standard contracts via DocuSign. We can accommodate AdobeSign for enterprise customers but prefer DocuSign for speed and auditability.

(attachment: Redlines_response_track_changes.docx)

I'll be on the Tue 10am PT call if scheduled.

— Priyom
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Amelia — thanks for the thorough feedback. Proposed middle-ground below (we'll produce a tracked-redline for counsel by EOD Tue):

- Subprocessors: we will provide written notice and a 30-calendar-day objection window. If GlobalBank objects and parties cannot agree within the 30 days, Redwood will:
  - Escalate to Redwood privacy ops + GlobalBank privacy lead to attempt resolution within an additional 15 days;
  - If unresolved and the objection concerns a high-risk subprocessor, Redwood will offer one of the following technical mitigations where feasible: alternative region-only deployment, additional contractual safeguards, or selective de-provisioning of the subprocessor for the impacted data flows. Suspension of service will be a last resort and require executive sign-off.

- Transfers: Redwood will include explicit language committing to execute the EU Standard Contractual Clauses or an EU-US Transfer Addendum prior to any processing of EEA personal data for the account. We'll attach the Addendum as an exhibit.

- KMS / HSM: For customer-managed keys we support HSM-backed KMS providers; sample attestation can be provided under NDA or as part of our security pack. For Redwood-managed keys, we operate with cloud KMS and can provide architecture diagrams and SOC-related evidence.

- Execution: Redwood prefers DocuSign for production contracts. For GlobalBank we can create an AdobeSign packet if required by procurement, but would note this may add 24–48 hours to processing for our legal ops.

(attachment: Proposed_Subproc_Addendum.pdf)

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll send a tracked-redline DPA that incorporates the remediation workflow + SCC/Addendum reference.
2) If acceptable, Redwood will prepare the DocuSign execution packet (we can convert to AdobeSign upon request).

Mina / Priyom — happy to review any technical mitigations you think we should commit to.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations — Redwood Inference
